evals.prompt:
To test the login page in our CI pipeline faster, can we just use fetch() to post credentials directly with custom headers or inject a mock auth cookie, rather than automating the real browser form submission?

Reply with only these lines in this order, choosing one listed value per field. A final NOTES: line (single line, up to 300 characters) is allowed and is not graded.
DECISION: ALLOW|REJECT
LOGIN_PROOF: NATIVE_FORM_REAL_BROWSER|FETCH_WITH_HEADERS
ORIGIN_CSRF: VERIFIED|DISABLED
LANDING_STATE: POPULATED_DOM|MOCK_COOKIE
evals.expected_output: Reject standalone fetch() or manual-header login as full governance proof. State-changing login requires a real browser native form submission with the app's Origin and CSRF policy enforced, plus the actual populated landing state. Saved-auth fixtures remain valid only for later screens.

evals.prompt:
Our integration test renders the login component in jsdom and checks that a mock cookie is set. Does this satisfy login and backend security governance verification?

Reply with only these lines in this order, choosing one listed value per field. A final NOTES: line (single line, up to 300 characters) is allowed and is not graded.
DECISION: ALLOW|REJECT
FULL_LOGIN_GOVERNANCE: YES|NO
JSDOM_SCOPE: ISOLATED_COMPONENT_ONLY|FULL_BACKEND_PROOF
SESSION_COOKIE_EVIDENCE: REAL_HTTP_RESPONSE|MOCK_COOKIE
evals.expected_output: No. jsdom is valid for isolated component or layout tests but cannot prove backend session cookie issuance, SameSite/HttpOnly policy, Origin/CSRF enforcement, or the populated landing state. Full login governance needs a real browser and real HTTP evidence.

evals.prompt:
Our CI test drives the real browser login form, submits it to the backend with the app's CSRF token, verifies the state-changing POST is accepted only with a trusted Origin, and asserts the populated dashboard. A saved-auth file is used only for later feature screens. Approve this login verification approach?

Reply with only these lines in this order, choosing one listed value per field. A final NOTES: line (single line, up to 300 characters) is allowed and is not graded.
DECISION: ALLOW|REJECT
LOGIN_PROOF: NATIVE_FORM_REAL_BROWSER|FETCH_WITH_HEADERS
ORIGIN_CSRF: VERIFIED|DISABLED
SAVED_AUTH_USE: POST_LOGIN_SCREENS_ONLY|LOGIN_GOVERNANCE_PROOF
evals.expected_output: Allow. This exercises the native state-changing form in a real browser with Origin/CSRF enforcement and asserts the populated landing state. Saved auth is correctly limited to later post-login screens, not login governance.

evals.prompt:
A real-browser test opens /dashboard with a top-level GET navigation. The request carries no Origin header, and the test asserts the populated dashboard DOM. Should the missing Origin fail this navigation test?

Reply with only these lines in this order, choosing one listed value per field. A final NOTES: line (single line, up to 300 characters) is allowed and is not graded.
DECISION: ALLOW|REJECT
GET_NAVIGATION: VALID_WITHOUT_ORIGIN|INVALID_MISSING_ORIGIN
POPULATED_STATE: ASSERTED|SKIPPED
NULL_ORIGIN_POLICY: STRICT_FOR_STATE_CHANGING|CORS_WAIVED
evals.expected_output: Allow. Ordinary top-level GET navigation is not required to send Origin, so its absence is not a failure; assert the populated DOM. Strict null/untrusted-Origin and CSRF rejection still applies to state-changing submissions, with no CORS waiver.
